hook: A standardized U.S. Navy Range Fouler Debrief Form documenting a nighttime visual encounter by an HSM-73 pilot with three unidentified small air contacts over the North Arabian Sea on August 24, 2020, notable for the contacts producing no electronic signature — no ES, no radar trackfile, and no IFF return.
why_it_matters: This report exemplifies the evidentiary challenge at the heart of UAP documentation: the objects were observed visually and described as having wings/airframe structure with metallic and reflective properties, yet left no electronic trace — no radar return, no emissions, no transponder signal. The appearance of two additional contacts to the east after the first disappeared behind a cloud raises questions about situational awareness and whether these were independent objects or a formation. As part of USCENTCOM MOR 26-0038 to 26-0046, this report entered the formal military disclosure pipeline and represents the kind of operator-level testimony that feeds institutional UAP analysis.

key_findings.finding: All three contacts produced no electronic confirmation — negative ES (electronic support/emissions detection), negative radar track, and negative IFF — making this a visual-only observation with no sensor corroboration.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This is a 2020 Navy UAP encounter report submitted through the SPEAR reporting pipeline and released as part of USCENTCOM MOR, exactly the category of operator testimony that AARO was established to collect and analyze.

MITRE supports DoD sensor and tracking analysis; the form's explicit notation of failed radar trackfile and sensor ambiguity is the type of technical gap MITRE-supported UAP analysis programs have examined.
